facts: These two appeals are filed against the judgment of High Court of Delhi in Criminal Appeal No. 324 of 1976 in which State of U.P. was the appellant.
The said appeal was filed against the judgment of acquittal passed by the 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Delhi in Sessions Case No. 2 of 1974.
In the said case six accused were tried for offenses punishable under Sections 120-B and 302 read with 34 IPC.
The trial court acquitted all of them.

In an appeal filed by the State against the said acquittal, the High Court convicted accused Girja Shankar Misra and Nathu Singh under Sections 120-B read with 302 IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life.
Nathu Singh was further convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to imprisonment for life.
One Girdhari, accused died during the pendency of the appeal.
The acquittal of the remaining accused was confirmed.

Accused Girja Shankar Misra has filed Criminal Appeal No. 272 of 1984 and accused Nathu Singh has filed Criminal Appeal No. 340 of 1984 in this Court under Section 2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act.
Since these are regular appeals, the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the State have taken us through the entire voluminous record and advanced elaborate arguments.
issues: Whether the prosecution has proved the conspiracy?
Whether the identification of Nathu Singh as one of the assailants by PWs 1, 7 and 9 can be relied upon?
Whether the High Court was justified in interfering with the judgment of acquittal?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution has miserably failed to prove the conspiracy.
The identification of Nathu Singh as one of the assailants by PWs 1, 7 and 9 cannot be relied upon at all.
Various irregularities in the test identification parade held.

Long and unexplained delay in holding the test identification parade throws any amount of doubt on the authenticity of the proceedings and the complaint of the accused that they were shown to the witnesses before being put up for the parade is well founded.
respondent_arguments: The High Court accepted some part of the evidence in respect of the conspiracy.
Girja Shankar Misra and Nathu Singh and Girdhari accused entered into a conspiracy to kill the deceased.
The presence of PWs 1, 7 and 9 could not be doubted at the time of occurrence and the identification of some of the accused by them could be accepted.
court_reasoning: We have carefully gone through the record and for the reasons stated we are of the view that the conclusions reached by the trial Judge on evidence are not reasonable and this compels us to interfere with the judgment of acquittal.
Our findings are-(a) That Girja Shankar Misra was at Hamirpur from 10th to 12th February.

holding: The High Court convicted accused Girja Shankar Misra and Nathu Singh under Sections 120-B read with 302 IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life.
Nathu Singh was further convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to imprisonment for life.
